title: Southern Chu
capsule: The Southern Chu (Ma Chu) was one of the Ten Kingdoms of the Five Dynasties period, carved out of Hunan by the warlord Ma Yin from the last years of the Tang dynasty and formalized when he received the title of king of Chu from the Later Liang in 907. Ma Yin and his successors administered Changsha and the Xiang River basin with relative stability for over half a century, promoting tea and silk production and maintaining a pragmatic neutrality among competing northern dynasties. Internal succession conflicts among Ma Yin's sons following his death in 930 fatally weakened the kingdom; the Southern Tang invaded and absorbed Chu in 951. The remnant rulers briefly recovered it in 956 before the Later Zhou and then Song incorporation completed the reunification of the region.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Southern Chu's Hunan-basin core territory is attested in Chinese dynastic sources; the precise extent of its jurisdictional reach into mountain frontier districts is uncertain.
